meta.el_note: NEGATIVE el only (belly view). Rows 0..-20 deg are the 2026-08-03 regenerated base; rows -24..-90 deg are the el-extension round, same convention and same mesh.
meta.quote_policy: percentiles/coverage only; NO null-min/sigma-min/aspect-peak/point value; m^2 linear mean (Jensen-optimistic, recorded)
meta.regenerated_from: shards: (drone x band) base rows + (drone x band x el) extension rows, src/experiment_freespace_sigma._sigma_grid_one
meta.regen_note: el 을 한 줄씩 잘라 부른 것 외에는 생산자 경로와 동일 — 3° 평활이 az 행 단위로 독립이라 여러 줄 일괄호출과 비트 동일하다. verify 라운드(vrfA)가 base 줄을 확장 워커로 재계산해 실증했다.
meta.el_rationale: New rows below -20 deg are placed from the MEASURED look-elevation density of the consumers (freespace_scene.look_el_deg over the published d x phi sweep, L=500 m, alt=60 and 120 m) and from a measured sigma(el) curvature probe (2.5 deg fine scan). Spacing widens from 4 deg near -24 deg, where 31 % of the out-of-range lookups sit, to 7 deg mid-range, then tightens to 3 deg below -78 deg where the nadir silhouette makes |dsigma/del| reach 4-10 dB per 2.5 deg. No positive el row: with the target above BOTH the 25 m illuminator mast and the 3 m receiver the bisector z-component is negative identically, so look el is strictly negative (max observed -0.13 deg).
meta.az_degenerate_note: At el = -90 deg the look vector is (0,0,-1) for every azimuth, so the row is one sigma replicated across az. That is correct monostatic physics, not a bug, but the row carries no azimuth averaging: if it lands in a null the whole row is a null. Do not quote per-azimuth statistics from it.
meta.multistatic_note: 옛 판의 multistatic 블록은 07-29 메쉬 낡음을 그대로 안고 있어 옮겨 싣지 않았다 — 필요하면 multistatic_check 로 재생성할 것.

anchor.statistic: azimuth LINEAR mean (10log10 mean sigma_m2) at el_ref, sigma_anchor.linear_mean_dbsm
anchor.relevel_crosscheck_note: conv_on branch must equal sigma_anchor.relevel() exactly; the production function is the oracle, not this replica
anchor.branch_note: The +2.5068 dB statistic-convention offset is a PURE LEVEL knob: it enters anchor_mu_dbsm as the same constant in every band. Under mode='slope_only' the production default it cancels EXACTLY (target = mu_anchor + (mean(mu_our) - mean(mu_anchor))), so both branches give bit-identical deltas. Under 'level_and_slope' it shifts every band by the same +2.5068 dB, i.e. it moves absolute R but cannot change which waveform wins. Report both branches anyway and lead with the slope, where it cancels.
